What exactly is Tic-Tac-Toe?

Tic-Tac-Toe is one of the world's best-known and simplest strategy games. It is played by two players on a game board with 3 × 3 spaces. One player chooses the symbol X, while the other plays with O. Players take turns placing their symbol in an empty space.

The goal is simple but surprisingly tactical: the first player to get three of their own symbols in a row – horizontally, vertically, or diagonally – wins the round. Smart play means not only building your own row, but also blocking your opponent at the right moment. The rules can be learned in under a minute, so both children and adults can join in right away.

SkillShot takes this familiar game to a whole new level. Instead of drawing symbols on paper, you must earn your X or O with an accurate throw. This turns a quiet pen-and-paper game into an active, sporty competition where skill is just as important as strategy.

Throw, spin, and get three in a row

SkillShot – Active & Challenging – Bean Bag 'Tic-Tac-Toe' Throwing Game turns a familiar strategy game into an active challenge. Choose your symbol, grab a bean bag, and aim at one of the nine rotating game blocks. With a well-placed throw, the block spins and reveals an X or O. Then try to be the first to get three of your symbols in a row horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.

But watch out: every new throw can change the game board. A clever opponent can turn a block, break up your combination, and suddenly move closer to victory themselves. This keeps every round exciting right up until the final throw.

Stay active and think strategically

With SkillShot, it's not just about being good at aiming. Just like in classic Tic-Tac-Toe, players also need to think about their next move. Will you focus on creating your own row, or try to block your opponent first? The combination of physical skill and simple strategy makes the game enjoyable for different age groups.

While throwing, children can playfully practice their hand-eye coordination, concentration, and accuracy. At the same time, the competitive element encourages adults to join in too. The result is an easy-to-enjoy family game where everyone has a chance to win.

Perfect for fun competitions with family and friends

Organize a one-on-one match, play several rounds, or turn it into a complete family tournament. SkillShot is easy to understand and quick to set up, making it a fun choice for play afternoons, children's parties, family nights, and other enjoyable moments together.

Thanks to its interactive game concept, children and adults can play together without complicated rules. Everyone knows Tic-Tac-Toe, so hardly any explanation is needed. Aim, throw, and try with every throw to get one step closer to three in a row.

products.body_html:
Make your own lollipops from real fruit, with less sugar and no artificial colorings!

With SweetPop, you decide exactly what goes into your child's treat. Fill the silicone lollipop molds with fruit puree, fresh juice, yogurt, or dark chocolate and make colorful lollipops in just a few simple steps, without the long ingredient lists found in packaged treats from the supermarket. 🍓

Make lollipops from real fruit, fruit puree, juice, or yogurt

🥄

You decide how much sugar goes in, or choose a sugar-free sweetener

No artificial colorings: color naturally with beetroot juice, turmeric, or blueberries

🧒

Helpful for allergies: you know exactly what is in the treat

Enjoy treats made with ingredients you choose yourself

Children want sweets, while parents want to know what is in them. With SweetPop, you no longer have to choose. Puree strawberries, mango, or banana and pour the mixture directly into the mold. Mix Greek yogurt with a little honey for creamy yogurt lollipops. Or melt dark chocolate and sprinkle it with nuts, coconut, or freeze-dried raspberries. You decide the portion size, sweetness, and color, and you can easily take lactose or nut allergies into account. Plus, the molds are small, so each treat stays a perfectly sized portion.

Ideas to get you started

  • Fruit lollipops: Puree fresh or frozen fruit, pour into the mold, and place in the freezer.
  • Yogurt lollipops: Greek yogurt with a little honey or maple syrup and pieces of fruit.
  • Smoothie lollipops: Use leftover morning smoothie, including spinach or banana.
  • Dark chocolate: Melt chocolate with a high cocoa content and add nuts or seeds.
  • Sugar-free option: Use stevia or erythritol instead of granulated sugar.
  • Natural colors: Beetroot juice for pink, turmeric for yellow, and blueberries for purple.

Fridge or freezer? Here's how to make them

Fill the mold, smooth the top, insert the sticks, and let the lollipops set. How long this takes and where the mold should be placed depends on the filling:

Filling Fridge or freezer Time Storage
Fruit puree or fruit juice Freezer 4–6 hours or overnight Freezer, 1–2 months
Yogurt with honey or fruit Freezer 4–6 hours Freezer, 1–2 months
Smoothie or mixed fruit Freezer 4–6 hours Freezer, 1–2 months
Melted dark or milk chocolate Fridge 20–30 minutes Cool and dark, several weeks
Chocolate with layers or filling Fridge 15 minutes per layer Cool and dark, several weeks
Gelatin or gummy mixture Fridge 1–2 hours Fridge, approximately 1 week
Date and nut mixture (no-bake) Fridge 30–60 minutes Fridge, approximately 1 week

Please note: Never place chocolate in the freezer. The chocolate will set too quickly and may develop condensation and white spots after thawing. Fillings with a high moisture content, such as fruit and yogurt, will not become firm enough in the fridge and should therefore be placed in the freezer.

Easy removal: Let a frozen lollipop sit outside the freezer for 1–2 minutes, then push it out of the mold from the bottom. This helps keep it intact.

Helpful tip: Place the filled mold on a cutting board or baking tray before moving it. Silicone is flexible, and otherwise the filling may spill over the edge.
